Topic: The Barber Pole Effect: Polarized Light in Sugar Solutions

Target audience: University Physics Students

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite: The Nature of Light

Lecture lines:
Light behaves as a transverse electromagnetic wave.
A polarizer acts like a vertical slotted fence.
Only light oscillating in the plane passes through.

Planned animations:
Create a static light wave propagating forward in #FFFFFF.
Add a vertical polarization filter in #FF00FF.
Show light restricted to vertical plane in #00FFFF.
Show rotation of the plane by a medium in #FFFF00.
Final state: rotated plane emerging from the medium.

Section: section_2 — The Mechanism: Optical Activity

Lecture lines:
Sugar molecules have a chiral, asymmetric structure.
These molecules force polarized light to rotate.
This rotation is known as optical activity.

Planned animations:
Display incoming polarized light in #00FFFF.
Introduce a chiral molecule rotating the light in #FF00FF.
Show the progressive angular shift in #FFFF00.

Section: section_3 — Creating the 'Barber Pole' Effect

Lecture lines:
We use a polarized light and sugar solution.
Light rotates differently based on its wavelength.
This creates a helical, barber pole pattern.
An analyzer reveals these vibrant color bands.
The cylinder appears as a stack of colors.

Planned animations:
Show multiple stacked polarizers at slight angles in #00FFFF.
Animate light passing through each, showing progressive rotation.
Highlight the resulting 'barber pole' spiral shape in #FF00FF.

Section: section_4 — Mathematical Visualization

Lecture lines:
Malus's Law dictates the light intensity output.
Varying sugar concentration changes the helix pitch.
A graph maps depth to rotation angles.
Periodic curves define the observed spectral colors.
Rotation correlates directly to sugar concentration depth.

Planned animations:
Represent the light vector with a rotating arrow.
Plot the sine and cosine components as wave functions.
Sum the vectors to show net linear path rotation.

Section: section_5 — Real-World Application

Lecture lines:
Polarimetry measures sugar concentration without samples.
Industries use this to maintain syrup quality.
Lasers verify batch concentration instantly, non-destructively.

Planned animations:
Show sugar solution inside a cylindrical test tube.
Project polarized light through the solution showing rotation.
Display the polarimeter reading the final angle.

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]

        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.play(vec.animate.rotate(PI/4))
